## The changing Balance of forces between Beirut and Damascus in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries

 Leila Fawaz 

 Revue des mondes musulmans et de la Méditerranée Année 1990 55-56 pp. 208-214 

 Fawaz Leïla. The changing Balance of forces between Beirut and Damascus in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. In: Revue du monde musulman et de la Méditerranée, n°55-56, 1990. Villes au Levant. pp. 208-214.

 Leila FAWAZ

 THE CHANGING BALANCE OF FORCES BETWEEN

 BEIRUT AND DAMASCUS IN THE NINETEENTH

 AND TWENTIETH CENTURIES

 In the course of the nineteenth century, Beirut imposed itself as the chief port on the eastern Mediterranean and as a center of political life for the Syrian region. In so doing, for the first time in its history, it gained ascendancy over Damascus and other cities of the Syrian interior, which it did not relinquish until after war broke out in Lebanon in 1975, and Damascus to a large extent regained its authority over Beirut. Over the course of history, the years when Beirut controlled the Syrian interior will not seem to be a very long time — only a hundred years or so, compared to the many hundreds of years between the seventh and the nineteenth century when the Syrian interior ruled the coast. But, however short-lived Beirut's ascendancy was, it came at a time when important changes were being wrought in the Middle East and Europe, changes so fundamental that by comparison the shift in balance back to the interior since the 1970s seems in no way as decisive. Nor is Damascus's ascendancy as likely to remain as unchallenged as it has been before the nineteenth century; the events of the intervening years have made that impossible. Here I propose to examine why that is so , by comparing the relative balance of forces between Beirut and Damascus in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, with the civil war of 1860 as the turning point in the relative position of both.

 Both Beirut and Damascus trace their roots to antiquity. Damascus prides itself on being among the oldest, if not the oldest, continuously populated city in the world.
